messages.author: 4b6a033bb73e401c
messages.subject: Every iteration hits max treedepth
parts:
Hi there

I'm trying to apply a model that I've got working to a different, messier dataset. As such I didn't necessarily expect NUTS to be successful, but what happened surprised me.

For 3 of the 5 chains, every post-warmup sample hit the max treedepth (as well as most pre-warmup samples). My understanding is that this means that the step size is too small, so each iteration doesn't reach the point of u-turning.

I'm trying to get a better understanding of NUTS, so I'd like to know what could have caused such a low step size to be chosen during warmup? 

Cheers
Sam

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Every iteration hits max treedepth
parts:
Just look at the step sizes — if they’re around 10e-16 then you know adaptation
messed up, which is probably due to some really pathological structure either in
the tails or even in the bulk (the latter requiring that the model be tweaked).
